_README: Manually-curated KH Nuclear Task Force practice notes. Keyed by NRC docket ID. The scraper merges these into rules.json on every run, so practice commentary persists across scrapes. Add `"manual": true` to include rules that aren't on the EO 14300 page.

NRC-2019-0062.title: 10 CFR Part 53 — Risk-Informed, Technology-Inclusive Regulatory Framework for Commercial Nuclear Plants
NRC-2019-0062.summary: Optional alternative to Part 50 / Part 52 for licensing commercial nuclear plants — risk-informed, performance-based, technology-inclusive. Final rule 91 FR 15696 published March 30, 2026; effective April 29, 2026. Headline provisions: alternative siting criteria (§ 53.530), factory fuel loading (§ 53.620), expanded use of consensus codes (§ 53.440), and new Part 26 / Part 73 frameworks for fitness-for-duty and physical security.
NRC-2019-0062.implication: The most consequential siting change in 60+ years. § 53.530 lets applicants site reactors in areas of higher population density — including centers of more than ~25,000 residents — contingent on a societal-risk-vs-societal-benefit demonstration. Directly enables the data-center and industrial-load colocation thesis that Part 100's distance-based criteria has historically blocked. Applications under Part 53 can be filed now. The 'societal risk vs benefit' framework is undefined in regulation — that's where early applicant-side consulting work will live until Reg Guide 4.7 Rev. 5 fills the gap.

NRC-2025-1336.summary: Procedural cleanup of NRC's general rules of practice. Tightens timelines, removes obsolete steps, and aligns Part 2 procedure with current practice.
NRC-2025-1336.implication: Modest, but real: faster docketing and motion practice helps every applicant we'd support. Useful as one of the early proof points that EO 14300 work is moving.

NRC-2025-0479.summary: Sweeping removal of obsolete and superseded provisions across nearly every Part of 10 CFR. A direct final rule with partial withdrawal from January 2026.
NRC-2025-0479.implication: Compliance noise reduction — fewer dead-letter requirements to track during licensing-basis reviews. No siting or design impact, but worth flagging when clients ask whether EO 14300 is actually shipping.

NRC-2024-0044.summary: Modernizes the NRC's FOIA processing rules to reflect current practice and statutory changes.
NRC-2024-0044.implication: Low direct project impact. Relevant only when sourcing historical NRC documents for due diligence or siting research.

NRC-2025-1501.summary: Tightens the contested-hearing process under Part 2: clearer admissibility standards for contentions, firm scheduling, and limits on procedural delay tactics.
NRC-2025-1501.implication: One of the highest-leverage rules in the package for project finance certainty. The open-ended hearing process has historically been the single biggest schedule risk for new build. Once final, this materially de-risks COL/CP timelines for hyperscaler-backed projects and any client building near contested communities.

NRC-2023-0212.summary: Annual update to NRC fee schedules under Parts 170 and 171, recovering the agency's budget through licensee fees.
NRC-2023-0212.implication: Direct input to client cost models. The FY26 hourly rate and annual fee structure feeds into licensing budgets and developer pro formas — track for any project doing financial sensitivity work.

NRC-2025-0379.summary: Creates a tailored, lower-burden licensing framework for microreactors and small, factory-built reactors with low offsite-consequence profiles. Affects EPZ sizing, staffing minimums, and security force requirements.
NRC-2025-0379.implication: Highest direct relevance to industrial and data-center off-grid power siting. If finalized roughly as proposed, opens the door to colocated microreactor deployment with realistic emergency planning footprints — a precondition for most factory and AI campus use cases we evaluate.

NRC-2026-0166.summary: Revises aircraft impact assessment requirements for new reactor applicants under Part 50.
NRC-2026-0166.implication: Affects design-basis assumptions and structural protection requirements for new builds — relevant during conceptual siting and security-by-design conversations with developers.

NRC-2025-1205.summary: Updates byproduct material licensing — industrial radiography, well-logging, and similar uses — to reduce administrative burden.
NRC-2025-1205.implication: Low direct relevance to nuclear power deployment. Worth tracking only for clients with materials licenses adjacent to project sites.

NRC-2025-1238.summary: Revises Part 37 security requirements for high-activity radioactive materials, focused on reducing duplicative compliance while preserving security objectives.
NRC-2025-1238.implication: Tangential to most Task Force work. Relevant for clients handling Cat 1/2 sources at industrial facilities.

NRC-2025-1370.summary: Broad modernization of NRC's materials licensing process across Parts 30, 40, 70 and related rules — application content, renewal cadence, and review timelines.
NRC-2025-1370.implication: Not directly tied to reactor siting or data center power, but worth monitoring for fuel cycle and front-end fuel facility clients.

NRC-2025-1503.summary: Allows NRC to credit safety reviews and operational data from designs that have already been authorized by DOE (or DoD/DOW) when those designs come forward for commercial NRC licensing.
NRC-2025-1503.implication: Strategically important for the DOE-pathway developers — TerraPower, X-energy, Kairos, BWXT-class designs that have already cleared DOE authorization. Reduces duplicative review effort and could compress commercial follow-on timelines by a year or more for clients pursuing those designs.

NRC-2025-0478.summary: Aligns NRC's NEPA process with the Fiscal Responsibility Act and the 2023 CEQ NEPA reforms — narrows scope of environmental analysis, allows applicant-prepared environmental reports, and tiers reviews by significance.
NRC-2025-0478.implication: High relevance to KH's environmental side. Tightens what falls inside vs outside NRC's NEPA scope, which affects both review timelines and the EIS workload our environmental teams produce. Particularly important for siting work where the NEPA timeline has historically dominated.

NRC-2024-0218.summary: Modifies the Atomic Energy Act's foreign ownership/control/domination (FOCD) restrictions on commercial reactor licensees to provide a clearer exception pathway.
NRC-2024-0218.implication: Useful clarification for developers with foreign equity partners — relevant for SMR developers backed by international utility or sovereign capital who would otherwise face structuring friction.

NRC-2025-1502.summary: Codifies a first-of-a-kind (FOAK) versus nth-of-a-kind (NOAK) framework for the uncontested mandatory hearings required by Section 189a of the Atomic Energy Act. Allows scaled-down hearings for repeat designs.
NRC-2025-1502.implication: Big procedural lift for fleet-deployment strategies. Once the first license for a given design is in hand, follow-on units face a much lighter hearing process — directly relevant to multi-unit data center campuses and any developer pursuing standardized deployment.

NRC-2025-0975.summary: The umbrella rewrite. Touches Parts 2, 50, 51, 52, 54, 71, and 100 — staged licensing, risk-informed oversight scaling, expanded siting flexibility (Part 100 reactor site criteria), decommissioning timelines, and inspection/reporting rationalization. Proposed rule projected late June 2026; final expected late 2026.
NRC-2025-0975.implication: The single highest-leverage rule in the EO 14300 package, and the one most likely to define how new nuclear actually deploys this decade. Carries the Part 100 site-criteria rewrite that Part 53 § 53.530 only addresses for the optional advanced-reactor track — meaning this is what unlocks higher-density siting for the operating fleet, Part 50 / Part 52 applicants, and any non-Part-53 new build. Read in full when proposed. Touches every aspect of Task Force work: siting, EP, oversight, decommissioning, and data-center colocation pathways.

NRC-2025-1237.summary: Streamlines Part 35 medical use licensing for radiopharmaceuticals and medical devices.
NRC-2025-1237.implication: Outside the Task Force's primary scope. Track only if a healthcare-sector client has adjacent licensing exposure.

NRC-2025-1140.summary: Broad reevaluation of Part 20 radiation protection assumptions, dose limits, and exposure standards — the foundation for emergency planning zones, occupational dose, and effluent control.
NRC-2025-1140.implication: Foundational. EPZ sizing, dose-based siting analysis, and operational exposure budgets all flow from Part 20. Outcome shapes how tight a microreactor or SMR can be sited next to a data center load center, and what kind of public-dose argument is required for industrial siting.

NRC-2025-1204.summary: Updates monitoring requirements for in-situ uranium recovery operations and tightens decommissioning timeliness rules across affected parts.
NRC-2025-1204.implication: Most relevant for upstream fuel-cycle clients and uranium recovery operators. Indirect relevance to reactor siting via the decommissioning timeliness piece.

NRC-2025-1667.summary: Updates Part 71 transportation package certification requirements for radioactive materials, including spent fuel and HALEU.
NRC-2025-1667.implication: Relevant for HALEU supply chain and any project requiring novel fuel transport. Touches transportation engineering work where radioactive material logistics intersect with route planning.

NRC-2025-1303.summary: Revises Part 73 physical security and Part 26 fitness-for-duty requirements — including security force size, design-basis threat assumptions, and access authorization.
NRC-2025-1303.implication: Big lever for microreactor and SMR economics. Current security force requirements were calibrated for large LWRs and add disproportionate operating cost to small reactors. A risk-informed scaling here is potentially decisive for sub-50 MWe siting at remote industrial loads.

NRC-2025-0643.summary: Aligns NRC's non-procurement debarment and suspension procedures with current government-wide standards.
NRC-2025-0643.implication: Administrative cleanup. No project-side impact unless a client is navigating a debarment matter.

NRC-2025-1138.summary: Cross-cutting enhancements to reactor licensing, decommissioning planning, and operational oversight under Parts 50, 52, and related rules.
NRC-2025-1138.implication: Important for the operating fleet uprate work — touches license amendment process and operational oversight scaling. Also affects decommissioning planning timelines for plants entering retirement.

NRC-2025-1468.summary: Updates Part 110 export licensing rules for nuclear equipment, materials, and components.
NRC-2025-1468.implication: Relevant for developer supply chains and U.S. vendors selling abroad. Tangential to siting and engineering work but worth flagging for clients with international deployment ambitions.

NRC-2025-0974.summary: Removes mandatory ACRS review for routine licensing actions, focusing committee attention on novel or safety-significant issues only.
NRC-2025-0974.implication: Procedural compression for the licensing review path. Removes one of the predictable schedule-extending steps for repeat designs and standardized applications. Combined with the FOAK/NOAK hearing rule, materially shortens the review tail for nth-of-a-kind deployments.

NRC-2011-0012.summary: Long-running rulemaking (since 2011) modernizing Part 61 low-level waste disposal requirements. Now folded into the EO 14300 package.
NRC-2011-0012.implication: Affects waste handling economics at decommissioning sites and plant operations. Relevant to operating fleet clients and any decommissioning advisory work.

NRC-2025-1568.summary: Updates the categorical exemptions from materials licensing requirements.
NRC-2025-1568.implication: Limited project-side relevance. Tracked for completeness.

NRC-2025-1139.summary: Aligns NRC procedures with the Federal Advisory Committee Act, plus access and security cleanup.

NRC-2025-1270.summary: Implements the February 2026 NRC reorganization (three core business lines: New Reactors, Operating Reactors, Materials & Waste) in the Code of Federal Regulations.
NRC-2025-1270.implication: Codifies the new NRC organizational structure that all licensing interactions will flow through. Useful context when explaining to clients which staff group reviews their application.
